**Vera Barbosa** (born 13 January 1989 in Vila Franca de Xira) is a Portuguese track and field athlete.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Barbosa#cite_note-2) She initially competed for Cape Verde, switching to represent Portugal after 2008. At the [400 metres hurdles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_400_metres_hurdles "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 400 metres hurdles") event at the 2012 Summer Olympics, in the heats she set a new national record with 55.22 seconds.

## About
Vila Franca de Xira is a city and municipality in the Lisbon District in Portugal. The population in 2021 was 137,659, in an area of 318.19 km2. Situated on both banks of the Tagus River, 32 km north-east of the Portuguese capital Lisbon, settlement in the area dates back to neolithic times, as evidenced by findings in the Cave of Pedra Furada. Vila Franca de Xira is said to have been founded by French followers of Portugal's first king, Afonso Henriques, around 1200.

## post by Roman_Ahmmed on Jan 4
Vila Franca de Xira is a city and municipality located in the Lisbon District of Portugal. It is situated on both banks of the Tagus River, approximately 32 km northeast of the Portuguese capital, Lisbon.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, on June 23, 2020, I visited Vila Franca de Xira for the first time. Since then, I have frequently returned, especially in the late afternoon, to enjoy its beauty.
The mural features António Alves Redol (1911–1969), an influential Portuguese writer and a key figure in the neo-realist literary movement in Portugal. Born in Vila Franca de Xira, his legacy is celebrated throughout the country for his significant impact on the cultural landscape of the 20th century.
You can find this type of mural in various parts of Portugal. The purpose of these murals is to showcase Portuguese culture and highlight prominent figures in the country’s history.
I really enjoy train journeys, and I have to take the train to reach my workplace along this route. It was during these travels that I discovered this place.
Sometimes, **I see local Portuguese people fishing with spears, which inspired me to get my own fishing license. I tried fishing a couple of times**, but I no longer come here due to my busy schedule.
**The best way to get from Lisbon to Vila Franca de Xira (Station)**.
Comboios de Portugal operates a train from Lisbon, Oriente Train Station to Vila Franca de Xira Train Station every 20 minutes. Tickets cost €2–14, and the journey takes 18 minutes.
Thank you to everyone for taking the time to read my entire post.
Happy guiding & stay safe!

## post by Roman_Ahmmed on Jan 4
Vila Franca de Xira is a city and municipality located in the Lisbon District of Portugal. It is situated on both banks of the Tagus River, approximately 32 km northeast of the Portuguese capital, Lisbon.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, on June 23, 2020, I visited Vila Franca de Xira for the first time. Since then, I have frequently returned, especially in the late afternoon, to enjoy its beauty.
The mural features António Alves Redol (1911–1969), an influential Portuguese writer and a key figure in the neo-realist literary movement in Portugal. Born in Vila Franca de Xira, his legacy is celebrated throughout the country for his significant impact on the cultural landscape of the 20th century.
You can find this type of mural in various parts of Portugal. The purpose of these murals is to showcase Portuguese culture and highlight prominent figures in the country’s history.
I really enjoy train journeys, and I have to take the train to reach my workplace along this route. It was during these travels that I discovered this place.
Sometimes, **I see local Portuguese people fishing with spears, which inspired me to get my own fishing license. I tried fishing a couple of times**, but I no longer come here due to my busy schedule.
**The best way to get from Lisbon to Vila Franca de Xira (Station)**.
Comboios de Portugal operates a train from Lisbon, Oriente Train Station to Vila Franca de Xira Train Station every 20 minutes. Tickets cost €2–14, and the journey takes 18 minutes.
Thank you to everyone for taking the time to read my entire post.
Happy guiding & stay safe!

## About
Vila Franca de Xira is a city and municipality in the Lisbon District in Portugal. The population in 2021 was 137,659, in an area of 318.19 km2. Situated on both banks of the Tagus River, 32 km north-east of the Portuguese capital Lisbon, settlement in the area dates back to neolithic times, as evidenced by findings in the Cave of Pedra Furada. Vila Franca de Xira is said to have been founded by French followers of Portugal's first king, Afonso Henriques, around 1200.
